So you may be asking yourself, what the hell is this HELI game?  It's really not a game at all.  It has three different apps.  Each app deals with exploring New York City.

1.  Guided 360 Helicopter Tours of New York.  The video quality is not the best I have ever seen, but still it's pretty good.  I enjoyed the tours of the five different sites.  They are short tours, but you get nice aerial views of the popular tourist spots.  The tours include 5 different spots:  Statue of Liberty, World Trade Center, Empire State Building, Central Park, and East River (i.e. Manhattan Bridge).  You basically circle around each one.  You can see things far off in the distance and since you're in high altitude, the people will look like ants.  I had never seen New Yourk in this way (and I've never personally visited), but I found the VR tours enjoyable.  You are seated in an empty helicopter and I guess you can pretend you're flying the helicopter (if you try really hard to imagine it, lol)

2.  Helicopter flying simulation.  Well, you should not get this app because of this feature.  It's very basic.  You use your motion controllers to fly the helicopter, but it is merely using the joystick on the Touch controller for altitude and the other joystick for direction.  That is the extent of the "flying".  You cannot crash.  The simulation also shows New York mostly as a model city would look.  Think mostly white blocks that represent the city layout.  So it's not the best graphics, but it gets the job done.  King Kong is at the Empire State Building, but he doesn't do anything to you and he doesn't seem to react to your presence.  This has potential to be better, but would need lots of updates.  At least the scale model of New York is spot on and I enjoyed that more than the actual simulation.  

3.  Garou Demo.  So basically this is a high resolution 360 photo from the Chrysler Building.  It is one of the best ones I have ever seen.  It's a still photo, but I thought it looked amazing.  

So that is it.  They advertise for more similar experiences on their website for the Garou Demo.  So is that all worth the asking price of $9.99?  That is a tough call.  I enjoyed the 360 helicopter guided tours.  But if you're not into it, then $9.99 may seem like a very steep price.  So if you want to experience the next best thing to an acual helicopter tour of New York, then this app is worth it.  Otherwise, pass on this.

Alright, here we go. This'll be a fairly short "review" after a rough playtime of seven hours and much, much regret. First off - I did not enjoy myself, but the people I played with had a significant resistance to nonsense and wanted to see if the game is even beatable in its current condition.

In case you're wondering: Yes, it's indeed beatable. Out of the... roughly 42 games we played, we've won one. All on easy, with roughly 3 people on average total. It didn't feel like a victory though, since all it boiled down to is sheer luck.

My main gripes with the game is probably what makes it so appealing to the eyes of the developers: the time limit, the lack of guidance and the disappointment of how much more useful the chalk could be if the only option you had wasn't a simple "x". Let's quickly go through these: the time limit is absolutely ridiculous. Even on easy, the maze is big enough so that you'll never be able to "map it out" even once anyway and that's assuming you [b]don't[/b] get lost, which you will, all the time. The only person that has partial immunity to getting lost is whoever is lucky enough to get hold of the chalk at the beginning, but even so, it boils down to marking dead ends all the time which, if you're unlucky, might not even have been dead ends in the first place since the first lever you need to pull removes one of the walls in front of the exit! (What a fun idea!) There will be games where you won't even find a single lever in 10 minutes, then there are some where you start out close to one, but still don't manage to find the other - it's a ridiculous predicament. Talking about randomization for a second, this shouldn't be a thing. If you have a team that sort of "knows what it's doing", then success or failure should be fairly consistent as a result. I don't expect to win everytime, but right now, whether we even find a single lever is not up to our skill, but to a roll of the die. Similarly, the developers expect you to make choices on whether it's smarter to sneak or hide, rather than run, but in practice, there is no choice: You always make a run for it. There's simply no time to waste and most enemies can be avoided so easily by just... running, that it's pointless to do any more anyway. 

Secondly, the lack of guidance is just ridiculous. Sure, it's supposed to be this gigantic maze where you just get lost and if that's the kind of thing the devs wanted to accomplish, then congratulations, it worked! It's just not fun - there is nothing you can go off, no clues, no hints, nothing. Perhaps it's easier to clarify, I'm talking about the sorts of hints that could give you slight sense of direction, perhaps there are markings on walls, or you could see faint light *above* the levers that you can see even when you're a tad farther away. Sure, it doesn't help you get there at all,  but at least you know where you're attempting to go! As I've mentioned before, right now, there is absolutely no way to know which way is correct. enemies can be anywhere, the people you're looking for are camping the levers for the most part (especially fun in dead ends!) and there's nothing you can do apart from marking every single dead end and slowly making your way through maybe a third of the labyrinth  before the time runs out. On easy. I'll talk about the strategies my group attempted to use a bit later on, so bear with me.

The last point I want to speak about a little bit are the items. They're god awful, but why? Two of the items serve a very specific purpose: stun a very specific monster. The stick is alright at doing its job, but mostly because the creature it protects you against is very vicious in the first place. Now if there was any point in sticking together, that'd be a cool feature, but right now, when you don't have a stick and encounter one or two after turning a corner, you're pretty much done if you haven't saved up stamina or are just plain lucky. Now for the flashlight: it's completely pointless. While you don't see much in the dark, that usually doesn't matter at all and the enemy it's supposed to protect you against is easier dealt with by just running away. It literally cannot kill you as long as you're running and it's not really giving chase either. It's just a very pointless piece of equipment to begin with. Now on over to the general-purpose tool, the infinite stone bag. It pretty much helps against every single monster appart from the ones that can only be beaten by the stick and redirects them towards the impact point of the stone for a few split seconds, if even. This is useful in a variety of situations, so not much to complain here. As for the last item, the chalk, it's ridiculous. Since you can only place "x", there's only one real function it can serve: marking dead ends. And that's about it! Why wouldn't we be able to draw arrows, or different signs, if feasible even free drawing for more useful, customised notes to potentially mark pathways we *wanted* to take, but couldn't just yet, or ones that might have a crossroad we haven't fully explored? It would make a very mediocre item that much more useful, but apart from that, it'd be neat if more than just one of the group could have it. The reason being, that literally everyone who doesn't have the chalk will get lost, eventually, while the chalk player happily creeps along at a snail's pace, but can still get lost when chased, which is fun, but rarely happens.

Before I finish this quick (...intended) nagging off with some pointers that *could* potentially be implemented, allow me to say what we did and why I arrived at the previous conclusions. Our group of 3-4, once comfortable, had just one strategy. Everyone grabbed an item, (with three people, whoever got the flashlight also had the chalk) and we made a run for it. At every crossroad, we'd split up to quickly search for dead ends that if found, could be marked down with chalk. Now while this sounds like a pretty insane strategy (just sprinting around the maze the entire time) it's currently the only feasible one. You simply don't have time for strolling about or building any sort of atmosphere, you just run. Enemies get ignored (you can run away from most of them anyway, even without a fitting item) and the only time where cooperation becomes sort of necessary is when one of the levers is in a dead-end. It sounds simple, not necessarily fun (it really wasn't, just a grind to maybe one day getting lucky, which we did once) but it lead to the result of beating it once. The ending really has no impact either, but at least it's there, so that's good.

It's interesting, the way things change over time. "No, I am your father" was a groundbreaking twist back when it came out, now it's almost a joke. MewnBase has been in development for 9 years if I understand correctly, and it was conceived in 2015 - and the developer's been working on this game in his spare time.

And, yknow, maybe if this indeed came out in 2015, it would've been fun. It's not awful even now, it did manage to hold me for 3 hours which is quite impressive, but I noticed that I'm getting bored roughly halfway through.

And that's the problem. It's just boring. Slow. Clumsy. The components of the game don't work together too well, and some features - such as things breaking - seem to serve no purpose other than to give you something quick to do. 

It's hard to even give legitimate criticism here. The randomly generated planets are, well, randomly generated, which almost always makes them uninteresting - we've known that for years now. And you need to walk around quite a bit, because you need a lot of resources to get a base going. That's not a bad thing if collecting the resource is fun. It isn't.

It's strange. All the elements seem decently polished, it looks neat, I love the art style, and it definitely feels like there's some design philosophy to it. But... not quite, or at least I don't see it. Perhaps most importantly, the game doesn't really flow. You know? There are just too much tedium between the interesting moments, and when they're interesting, they're not even that interesting.

God, this game's turned my brain into mush. Even this review sucks. Oh well. Perhaps that's a good sendoff to this whole thing.

First of all, I'd like to say that I've been playing Slay.one for hours on end on the browser version, which is honestly more worth playing on than buying the game on Steam.

I've played Slay.one for a whlie now, and I have to say, that it's a really fun game. However, this is completely overshadowed by the laggy servers, countless glitches, and redundant gameplay. I used to love this game. A lot. But that was when the devs actually cared about the game and its community. Now, most of the players you'll find not even talking to one another, and most of the interaction between people will be salt between multiple players. The ELO (ranked) system of the game is completely broken, and can easily be manipulated to either lower someone's ranking on the ELO boards, or make someone's ELO higher, which brings complete unbalance to the game itself. Hell, 95% or more of the users on the ELO board are either extremely inactive, or quit the game entirely (mainly because the lack of quality updates and redundancy of the game). If my paragraph of complaints didn't bore you enough, I'm just gonna list off all of the broken features/downfalls of the game.

1. The devs never communicate with the community, and even when they do, they'll only usually interact with the most boring/useless posts of the Slay.one subreddit. They completely fail to receive complaints and only seem to make Slay.one worse and worse as time goes on.

2. The "Infection" mode of the game is pretty much broken. There's no teamwork aspect of it at all because if you end up teaming up with someone you'll most likely end up dead, and it pretty much ruins the entire gamemode entirely.

3. Custom builds have been removed, which means you can't choose your own loadout, and the only gamemode you can use custom builds in is Normal Deathmatch (which barely anyone plays, by the way. You'll find arenas completely filled up with bots.).

4. The updates take months to come out, and when they do come out, they're usually full of glitches that failed to be fixed in a timely fashion. An example of this is the April 3rd update, which completely ruined the game with a gamebreaking bug that would glitch out your entire screen (by the way, that update took months to come out and somehow the devs didn't do anything about it until 2 weeks+ later.).

5. The devs fail to fix glitches that have been here for way too long (e.g. invisible walls).

6. The ELO system is completely broken, and has been completely broken ever since it came out. The ELO system never changed, and Ranked Deathmatch consists of things called ELO Assassins, which kill people with a high ELO, and drag their score down for no apparent reason.

7. Their is an epidemic of teamers in the Normal Detahmatch/Ranked Deathmatch modes, and it completely ruins the points of these gamemodes, and these people never seem to be punished.

8. A lot of the maps for each and every gamemode aren't even in the voting pool for the next round, and that renders the maps completely useless, because if you mad a match on your own, no one would join.

9. There are turret spammers everywhere littered into the game, who just spam turrets anywhere and everywhere, and it's completely unbalanced.

10. There are virtually no moderators to enforce the rules of the game, which means there are trollers/rulebreakers everywhere, and they completely ruin the gameplay experience.

11. Chests are completely luck-based, and don't encourage players to do their best in a game, and the game generally lacks an incentive to get chests (because you can just AFK in a match for 5mins and get a chest, How fun!). The chests are completely lackluster.

12. Clans are completely useless, because there are no rewards at all for being in a clan, besides getting on the leaderboards (which is a waste of effort, honestly.). Also, because the clans depend on the ELO system for their scoring, the clans system is completely broken as well.

13. The game lags frequently, and the servers suck, which can easily ruin gameplay.

Well, that's all I'm going to cover now, I'll edit this some other time and add some more issues with the game. I cannot at all recommend this game, because of the countless issues with it, and the almost completely inactive devs. 

If you want to see more (and valid) complaints about this game, just check the top posts of all time in the SlayOne subreddit, you'll see.

[i] My Experience [/i]

I'm a big fan of co-op stealth games, although there aren't all that many around. My co-op partner and I had a lot of fun recently playing Aragami 2 on Microsoft's GamePass for PC. This particular game reminded me of [b]Moonshot - The Great Espionage[/b], a game I played and had a good time with last year.

Unlike [b]Moonshot[/b], there doesn't seem to be a way to incapacitate enemies for the duration of the level in [b]Haste Heist[/b]. However, you do have the option to trip them up on a banana peel (briefly stunning them), or lure them away to go and eat a delicious donut (off of the floor, haha).

[b]Haste Heist[/b] is also generally good at giving the player(s) the information necessary to make good stealth decisions. You can generally tell when you'll be seen and how much noise you are making when you make the risky decision to sprint.

Where the game fell apart for us was with the bugs. When you are spotted, enemies madly dash around the level looking for intruders. This is fine, and makes sense. However, these previously patrolling enemies will sometimes then park themselves in front of doors that you are required to pass through in order to complete the level. On other occasions, previously patrolling enemies will get stuck repeatedly going up and down the same staircase between two floors after responding to an alarm. Lastly, we recently made it to the end of the yacht level only for our characters to pop out on the left side of a staircase and get stuck with no access to the exit rowboat. We restarted the level, but this happened again! When a game is slow and methodical by nature, having to restart a level due to bugs is particularly painful.

The "bones" of the game are solid, but I just can't recommend it in its current state (at least to be played in co-op). However, if stability was increased I might end up having a good time here (despite still wishing that there were a few ways to incapacitate enemies for the duration of a level).

I have been quite involved in this game so take my review with a grain of salt.

We have been playing this game in big international couch co-op parties and every time it has been a blast! There is enough content for multiple parties too. And when the story of about 50 levels gets completed, there is steam speedrun leaderboards and the co-op to mess with. 

While the game might not be perfect in every way, I'm gonna give it a thumbs up for the good times!

This is a pretty fun update to the old Super Offroad game we all remember from arcades and NES.  There is a lengthy Career progression with tons of upgrades similar to the old games and more on top of that.  And despite having 2 different in-game currencies they are all earned from winning races or leveling up your character (not microtransactions!).  

There are also some nice mini-game events like the long jump and obstacle course that change it up from time to time.

One negative is that your truck starts off pretty slow, and it takes several races before you start to get a decent sense of speed.  It's good for getting used to the controls, but definitely makes you feel less excited to race at first.

I'm not a huge fan of the graphics effects...the lighting is a bit harsh and there are some line overlays on the trucks and things that make it all feel aliased/jaggy or something.  It's not bad by any means, especially from a team of this size, just slightly hard on the eyes if you pay attention to it.

My biggest complaint is probably the AI rubberbanding.  You're almost always better off sticking with the other drivers, because if you get too far ahead they're going to come boosting out of nowhere and blow your doors off as they win the race.  I wish this was toned down considerably to make them more competitive overall but less "come from behind" weiners.

Although there are a ton of upgrades, as far as I can tell you're limited to the one monster truck for vehicles.  You can change color and get liveries for it, but you won't be changing into buggies or stadium trucks or anything if that matters to you.

Overall, I'd definitely recommend this if you want something like the old Super Offroad.  Support a tiny indie team! The developer has been super responsive to bugs and suggestions, and hopefully that continues with polishing the game even further!

I think what this game primarily lacks is the "Devil in the details".
I bought the game after the 2.2 update and so comparing the new features to the reviews listed here prior to mine, I can get an idea of what's been improved.
HOWEVER, I believe there are still core elements of the game that should be addressed in order for it to make more sales, here's my outline:


PRO:
* I think the engine of the game is alright; the steering needs tightening and perhaps some more collision consequences to the AI but otherwise it's OK.


CON:
(starting from the beginning of the game)

* MENU/GUI: The Menu is antiquated for today's standards; the giant buttons, no controller support for the menu - feels like it was quickly added in once the game engine and tracks were made, because it's obligatory to have a menu system, etc.

* UPGRADES VS LIVERY: so there are a 2 main currencies in the game:
 - (green) vehicle upgrades
 - (yellow) vehicle upgrades (mystery box style) and for decals/skins
because the (yellow) currency can be used for vehicle upgrades, there is no practical benefit to using them for skins, plus the visual prettiness costs a lot, for what you potentially get in return for spending it on performance instead.
 - I think this can be fixed by either separating the 2 currencies to be exclusive OR make visual bonuses to be awarded for winning/special plays, events, etc etc.

* MULTIPLE EVENT TYPES OVER RACING: this is less of a fault and more of a personal preference but I'v believed racing games should be about racing events with other racers; as opposed to time trails, slalom driving, stunt jumps and so on. I believe people are here to race opponents, not race themselves or challenge cement wall-dodging. If there is a real need for these extra events then I would say put them in a separate game-mode; and they can be utilised there and out of the way - but as I say, I'm not sure if I'm the minority on that one.

* 2ND CHAPTER: So the first chapter introduces your adversary (kind of like NFS Hot Pursuit) and then you go through a series of events until you finally compete with them. The 2nd Chapter seems to just be a series of buttons to each event and then congrats you for beating the 2nd Adversary and then continues to normal going into the 3rd event - did the devs forget to setup a graphical map/interface for the 2nd Chapter? This is one of those examples that needs polish.


I've noticed the Devs have updated some of the reviews which makes me think they genuinely care about the game and its playerbase; I'm putting this much detail into the review, not because I want to be a jerk but in hopes to help the Team in where they might improve, because I honestly think there is something within this game that can be better used, with time and patience and I think if the Devs have a look at some other racing games and their layouts, I reckon they could iterate some core aspects (particularly menu GFX and economy balance) and improve on a massive amount of detail with just small but very deliberate changes.

I bought SuperTrucks when it first came out, it was a cool game but a little rough around the edges. The Dev (a one man team I believe) has made quite a few HUGE updates over the past several months and I'm finding the game even more fun to play.

I have been playing the 'Career' mode (have not tried MP yet), but you do get screen notifications when a MP game is available - just waiting to get a little better before trying MP.

With Career mode you start in 1 city that has many racetracks, all tracks but 'one' are locked. You need to 'win' the race on that track before the next track unlocks and then you work your way through all the races until the final track - where you race the 'Champion' for that city. When you beat the Champion the next city is unlocked and rinse/repeat the process. Also, as you race there are 'pickups' on the track; extra Nitrous, money bags, cards and chance for SuperCrates. (the Cards have pictures of Truck parts on them, these are used in the shop to upgrade your Truck - SuperCrates contain multiple cards)

The game has a Shop where you can upgrade the various sections/parts (which start at Tier 1) for your Truck, there is also a 'Customize' area where you change the Paint, Tires and Decals (I think) - these Customize options become unlocked by 'leveling' your Truck or they can be obtained (unlocked at least) by getting a random bonus with the SuperCrates (they still need to be bought, once unlocked). Duplicate parts and high-tier parts (that you cannot use) can be sold from the Shop window - just double-click the card.

The in-game currency is 'money' $$ and Gold - spend the Gold wisely it does not come as easily as the money, you will get money every time you race - win or lose. You can also buy SuperCrates (from the Shop) in the hopes of getting some parts for your Truck to upgrade, there is also a chance to 'Unlock' a new 'Customize' option. 

There are 3 daily challenges that allow you to earn some extra money, the challenges (so far) have been the same three; Distance Jump, Obstacle Course and a Timed Race.

The Dev has been actively supporting this game over the last 3-4 months making a lot of positive changes, has been responsive on the Forums and is open to ideas/suggestions to improve the game.

I have been having a lot more fun with the game since all the recent updates and so I recommend the game. At only $10 I think it's worth a try and if you're not sure you can refund - I think you will know within 2 hours if you like the Arcady type of fun this game offers.

Starfighter Neon is an unabashed, lazy ripoff of games such Asteroids/"SpaceWar!" (Copyright Atari/Steve Russell respectively, 1980/1962 respectively).  Many lazy "amateur" developers don't pay attention to their obligations under copyright law, and often steal the ideas of actual, real game developers without credit, such as the "developer" here has done.  At this stage no legal action has been taken by Atari/Steve Russell respectively against the "developer" here, but it's never off the table, as previous copyright law cases have shown.

Putting aside the unethical intellectual bankruptcy of stealing someone else's game concept for profit, this is also breaking that unwritten law of stealing other people's game ideas... you should at least try to do better than the game you're ripping off.  Starfighter Neon is considerably worse than Asteroids/"SpaceWar!".   You can play Star Control 2 for free, and that's way superior to any of those games, and a million times better than this trashware.  The developer expects you to pay them money for this, by the way. 

From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.

The graphics here are some of the worst, laziest attempt at video game "art" I've ever seen.  It's hard to suggest this game even has graphics.  It's just untextured, basic pixel blocks and blobs, the kind that an infant child might be able to create in 5 minutes on MS Paint.  It's clear the developer didn't even try to produce any real graphics for the game and just phoned it in.  It's unclear why such a lazy approach was taken, whether it may be caused by lack of talent, budget, or motivation to do their job properly.  It also doesn't matter... what matters is that this has resulted in a game with zero visual appeal for gamers.  It's an immediate failure on that measure alone.

While there are options to change the resolution for the game, all this does is scale up the simplistic 2D art assets used to make the game, which makes little or no difference to the graphics quality.  Without any other substantial graphics tweaks, it's not possible for gamers to improve the lacklustre 2D visuals.

The controls can't be customised (although you can flip between a couple of control schemas, all bad), which will be an annoyance for many, but it can also render the game unplayable for differently-abled gamers, or gamers using AZERTY or other international keyboard layouts.  

These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.

The poor quality of this game is reflected by how many people spent time with it.  At the time of this review, SteamDB shows the all-time peak player number was only 2 players.  This is a remarkably low number, and now, the only player activity occurs once or twice a month, presumably someone loading it up to see what it is then quickly uninstalling it.  Considering there's over 120 million gamers on Steam and well over 50,000 games for gamers to choose from (over 9,000 completely free titles), the overwhelming lack of interest in this low quality game is to be expected.

Starfighter Neon is relatively cheap at $1 USD, but it's not worth it. Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.

The products that result from asset flips aren't "real" games.  They lack depth and content, because they're just simplistic copies of demos or tutorials.  In this case, "Top Down Shooter Characters Pack" is just an asset pack with characters to be used in top down shooters, combined with a very simple demo to show how to use them in a real game, and doesn't have any merit as a proper, fully fledged PC game, so a copy+paste of it can't be recommended.

Asset flips don't involve any professional game development.  Sure, sometimes they may change a few cosmetic things, swap out different assets etc, but at heart it's functionally identical to the asset they're ripping off.

Asset flips like this are harmful to the gaming industry and to Steam because they reduce the visibility that sincerely made indie games should have, and make it harder for gamers to find real games from genuine developers.

Don't reward this morally bankrupt, unethical behaviour from BitlockStudio/LillyWelland Inc.

Disclaimer:  I know the developers and was a beta tester for the game prior to early access. 

First Impressions: 
* This game is awesome!!!  It sort of reminds me of Mario Kart, but with the ability to play in VR as well. It is fast-paced, fun, and easy to pick up and play, but difficult to master. 

The Pros:
* Cross-Platform Multiplayer Support: I originally tried this game for VR, and was surprised to find that it's actually pretty fun to play on PC as well.   I love that you can play with your friends on both at the same time.  The controls and gameplay are different between the platforms, but they have done a very good job at balancing everything so that there isn't a clear advantage either way.

* Smooth VR Controls: One of the things that sets this game apart from other VR games is how smooth the controls and motion are. Every other game I have played that involves much motion has made me queezy, but somehow, even though this game is so quick-paced, it doesn't make me sick at all.

* Single Player: I tried out some of the solo challenges and thought I'd blow through them really quick, but the more difficult ones are actually quite challenging to complete, let alone get a score up on the leader boards.  They do get repetative though.  I'm looking forward to them adding more/different single player modes.

* Weapons/Items: I love the weapons and items so far, and I figured out that you can put most of them in the slingshot as well (like an empty rocket launcher). My favorite weapon in the game has to be the box of bees. I love how the buzzing sound instantly instills fear in me, and makes me run even if I'm about to down someone. I can't wait to see what weapons get added next.

The Cons: 
* Slow to find multiplayer match: It takes awhile to find a multiplayer match. I expect this is because it was just released and will get better once a player-base is built up.  They are planning to add bots soon, so this should be less of an issue once that's done.

* No player progression:  There isn't much for player stats, levels, unlockables, etc in the game right now.  It's fun to play online with friends, or maybe to load up and show off your VR setup to people, but there isn't much incentive to keep playing solo unless you like seeing your name on top of the leaderboards for the challenges.  

* Minor Bugs: I noticed a couple minor bugs so far, but they haven't crashed the game or anything like that. Once when I was downed, my basket got stuck on a pillar part way down so I didn't reach the ground. Another time when I used a shield ball, the shield went flying around the map.... come to think of it, maybe it was supposed to be that way... maybe some of the shields are intentionally defective.

I’m playing some weird games for VR and Mystery Stone from Heaven is a STRANGE mix of feelings, themes and graphics. You start the game with a Chinese narrative(no translation from what I could see). I frantically pushed buttons wondering if there was something to toggle but somewhere along the opening scene, translations began. Of course, the translations are Google Translate quality so there is some silly things such as “Prevent walking around in space with unprincipled from getting injured.” There is a lot of dialogue from the Simple Family – weird, cutesy out of place cartoonish characters who give you hints on the game. The game ironically has an inventory system that actually works(a backpack). There was a lot of objects that you could pick up but it seemed like it only required a select few to move on.

What is jarring about the game is the way the “style” changes. The animals that live in Mystery Stone from Heaven actually look quite great and out of place. They’re not cartoony and look quite intimidating although they pose no danger from what I could tell(maybe I could walk into them and die?) They seemed happy to sit there and snarl at me. For instance, the Scorpions look like something out of Skyrim but they’re in an education – low action game. It’s quite strange. The music is also quite varying – ranging from EPIC fantasy combat music as you shoot a bow which ends just as abruptly or the knock off Halo music when you begin the second area. There is a super long track when you summon a princess which sounds like something from a Final Fantasy game complete with a cool EDM track. The princess actually looks high quality and the effects used putting together the princess are actually really good and out of place for the rest of the game.

The actual length of the game seems to be about 20 minutes but to be honest – I’m not sure if I completed the game or not. I basically died, woke up in my office and the credits rolled. I’m not sure if the “death” was inevitable but I accepted my fate and shut off the game. The puzzles aren’t anything too difficult – just find a few objects, put them in a resurrection area and proceed. The second level caught me a little off guard and an accident revealed the way for me. With the HTC vive, it is impossible to move with something in that same hand for teleporting so that made a couple parts annoying(like shooting the bow) – maybe intentional or not.

I’m not sure I can really RECOMMEND buying a game like this unless you’re looking to be amused for a short time. The translations of Mystery Stone from Heaven might be enough for your enjoyment or the out of place music. Just don’t go in expecting a real game or story. Surprisingly, there wasn’t a terrible amount of bugs..ok, well the rhino running through the wall was funny but nothing game breaking. If it was a bit cheaper, I’d probably recommend it just for a “check it out” type game and maybe if its under $3-$4, it could be worth that price tag. I’ve certainly played shorter or worse games for a more expensive price.

Based on the real life suicide game, Blue Whale is a weird horror game that I don't know how to fully cover.

Story:

You play as Midori, a 12 year old girl. One day when returning home, she sits down next to her computer and opens up her social media, as she receives a message from the Blue Whale game, she is plunged deep into the game and you have one chance to save her.

As I said before, the game is heavily inspired by the real life Blue Whale game, where in some instances people did actually commit suicide afterwards. It's a sensitive topic to cover, but my morbid curiosity got really interested in checking it out and I'll say right now the plot in the game is really bland. The story is very hard to follow considering a lot of the times the translation is very poor. The notes you read seem to be written in a way to set up a very bleak tone and it works, cause the game is very depressing from start to finish, but it's all very cliche to say the least.

Graphics:

The art style is really decent, however I do have some minor gripes with it. Midori is a very cartoony looking character, she is very small and sort of resembles a character sprite out of a JRPG, but once you're plunged into the dark world, you run into other humans that look much more like real humans. I guess it's to set up a very surreal tone  which works, cause even the environments seem to wildly different from one another.

You can enter a house and see a giant eye looking at you instead of walls and not to mention how many locations you visit, like shopping districts, beaches, bridge crossings and other stuff. It's a very moody looking game and I did really like most of it.

Audio:

For the most part, the audio is decent enough. Every little audio cue does play up the atmosphere and when you're going down dark alleyways and start hearing rumbling and wind howling it is pretty creepy. However most sound effects are very likely to be royalty free cause I've heard them before, in some other horror games. They are used effectively so I won't nag on it too much.

Gameplay:

Blue Whale is more or less an adventure game where you explore your environments and solving very light puzzles, however as soon as the game begins, you're left on your own devices on figuring out how to actually do anything. Your main goal is to save Midori and you mainly do this doing moral choices, which are actually really cryptic in a way. 

When you die you are sent back to the start of the game and have to play from the start, as there's no checkpoints or a save system. This is one of the biggest negatives of the game, at least for me. It's not that bad since the game is bite size a single playthrough takes roughly 30 minutes, but it's still really annoying when you die because of something you didn't know can kill you and forced to start from the beginning.

The puzzles themselves mostly consist of trying to get to certain locations, which is both simple and fairly complex and tend to be really annoying to figure out, not to mention most of these endings are just really not that good and not worth playing the game multiple times.

Verdict:

Blue Whale is a really mediocre horror game. It has some decent scares and a really nice atmosphere, but everything else is just bland. The story is really hard to follow and just boring and the gameplay is just walking around trying to figure stuff out that is not made clear to the player. For some it might be worth checking out on a heavy discount, but other than that, just skip it.

Final Rating:
5/10

Pros:
+ Great atmosphere
+ Some decent scares

Cons:
- Story is not great
- Some endings are way too cryptic 
- Gameplay is really boring

Games can be art, if they're exceptionally well made.  Badly made art, shoved into a game-like format doesn't make "art" better, however, it just makes gaming worse, which is apparently the goal of the "developer" for this junk.

Trying to address social issues through the medium of video games is misguided and can be harmful.  While it's plausible to suggest the intention was noble, this can do more harm than good.  Game developers are not professionals in areas of mental health and social problems, and when they use video games to pretend they are, this can cause far more harm than good.  It's my opinion that it's improper to use video games to push political or social agendas.  Apart from the harm such hamfisted attempts at addressing social problems can cause, this offers zero benefit to PC gamers.  People suffering from health issues or other social problems should seek out professional help rather than going to crap shovelware video games attempting to get sales by exploiting such problems for their own benefit, as is the case here.

From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.

The game doesn't have any save game features, despite that being a basic standard for all games of this time.  The developer might defend this as an attempt to make the game seem more "difficult" without them having to balance the game or do their job properly with engaging and challenging level design, but it's just as likely they simply couldn't work out how to make a save game feature work.  Either way, that's a defect that adds another reason for gamers to avoid this game.

A choice was made to use obsolete, decades old retro pixel "art" as a substitute for contemporary PC graphics.  It's unclear if this is due to lack of budget or talent, regardless, the overall visual quality of the game is extremely low as a result.

There's no option to change the resolution and no useful graphics tweaks.  There's no way to ensure this is running at the native resolution of your display.  There's no guarantee this game will look right on any PC as a result of this hamfisted design decision.

The controls can't be customised, which will be an annoyance for many, but it can also render the game unplayable for differently-abled gamers, or gamers using AZERTY or other international keyboard layouts.  

Some of the defects in the game can be attributed to the choice of using the GameMaker Studio construction kit/toolset.  This is a very poor quality toolset favoured by amateur developers as it's cheap and requires little in the way of development skill, but unfortunately has very limited capabilities.  Just as you can't make a silk purse out of a sows ear, you can't make a great video game if you use a terrible engine.  GameMaker Studio is most commonly used to make retro pixel shovelware and cash grabs.

A strong argument can be made that construction kits like GameMaker Studio should never be used to make games for profit, as the "developer", Lissencephaly has done here.  These construction kits are intended to teach people some of the basic principles of game development, and to make small demos to pass around with friends.  They're not intended to replace to actual work of real, professional game developers.  So it's inappropriate when amateurs try to use these for profit, without any actual, real game development effort taking place.  This doesn't result in products that have any real meaningful value for gamers.

These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.

The poor quality of this game is reflected by how many people spent time with it.  At the time of this review, SteamDB shows the all-time peak player number was only 5 players.  This is a remarkably low number, and now, the only player activity occurs once or twice a month, presumably someone loading it up to see what it is then quickly uninstalling it.  Considering there's over 120 million gamers on Steam and well over 50,000 games for gamers to choose from (over 9,000 completely free titles), the overwhelming lack of interest in this low quality game is to be expected.

Blue Whale has the far too high price of around $4 USD, it's not worth it given the defects and shortcomings with the product, especially considering the sheer number of completely free, much higher quality games on Steam.

Card Crawl is an ingenious take on solitaire.  You play with a set of playing cards and 5 ability cards.  Each turn, you are dealt up to four cards, which can be treasure, monsters, weapons, potions, shields or ability cards.  Your hero has a set amount of hit points, and the object is to have all the cards dealt out of the deck, and still be alive.

There are 35 ability cards, and you start with a handful at the beginning of the game.  The rest are unlocked as you win the game and use in game currency to unlock them.  The better the card, the more expensive it is.

As you progress, you also unlock additional features to the game, as in choosing your ability cards beforehand (normally they are taken from your collection randomly); unlocking additional hero cards; and creating and playing other players' decks.  I've played a handful of them.  They're all over the place, from challenging to WTF were you thinking?!

It's well worth the cost, either on sale or no.  For a relaxing, casual card game, it's aces in my book.

Very fun, well crafted, simple game hampered by its unnecessarily grindy quest/unlock system.

You play against a random deck drawn from a fixed set of cards 49, and you get to choose 5 "ability" cards to mix in for a total of 54. The ability cards are fun, but you're heavily reliant upon the luck of when they show up.

You unlock more ability cards with credits you earn as you play. Credits earn decently fast and you can read card descriptions before you pick which one you want to unlock, so earning them is not bad at all.

The problem is the quests and achievements. They tend to be heavily luck based, and they require repetition so you're burying yourself in not only getting that lucky draw once, but 10 or more times. Some examples might help illustrate my point.

One is to beat the deck 10 times while throwing all 5 of your ability cards in the trash. The problem is even if you play perfectly, about half of the time the deck isn't beatable without using your ability cards. Beating it once this way was fun, having to grind through dozens of plays to accomplish it 10 times was not.

Another is to beat the deck 10 times with over 20 health. There's only 2 ability cards that give you more health, and they won't push you over 20 alone. You're reliant upon comboing with other ability cards that increase their value. So you're heavily reliant upon drawing a specific few cards in a specific order. It's possible but again to achieve this 10 times is going to take dozens of games.

It's frustrating knowing that you've played as best you can and you had absolutely no chance due to the shuffle of the cards - and you're going to have to do this over and over again until you get your lucky draw 10 times total. 

That being said, the quests and achievements do give you a reason to change your 5 ability cards in creative and fun ways. So conceptually they're great, I think the main problem is needing to do it 10 times.

I've had great fun with the game, but I think not everyone will find the same level of enjoyment, so I'm giving it a tentative thumbs up. If you can deal with luck based grind and you enjoy striving for achievements, then this might be a nice game for you. If not, you might want to skip it, since you'll likely get tired of the game within a few hours.

The basics are a simply card game, played in a tavern, to simulate a dungeon run.
The gameplay is basic, requiring a little thought and some basic math skills, nothing heavy duty but enough to engage.
The art is delightful, the artist should be doing children's books and board games for big bucks. 
The animation is cute, what little of it there is, but it is a bit hurky-jerky at points. 
The sounds are good, suiting the game well, without getting too repetitive, and the music is pleasant, in the background where it belongs, and simple.
The controls work fine, though not much is asked of them. Sometimes you have to be a little careful where the mouse pointer is, but nothing extreme.
The game builds in several minor ways. You can unlock special cards that give you nice abilities. These really  only serve as a goal though, and aren't really exciting. In fact this can work against you in the normal game, as the more you unlock the less your know what to expect from the cards, only five of them go into the deck, no matter how many you play.
There are a few other areas where you can play, one where you decide the five cards you want, one where you play against decks other players (I think) have made, a daily game which doesn't seem to offer anything special that I can see, and that's about it.
Wait, there is one more style of play, the dungeon delve. You go into successive dungeons, trying to win as many times in a row as you can. While challenging, it is a bit lackluster, you bring nothing forward from game to game, and before you can even play you've made money obsolete, as you have to have purchased all the ability cards to unlock delve mode.
The game has a few quests, which unlock different players and dealers from what I have gathered. The second player is exactly the same as the first, with different art. Not sure why more effort wasn't put into this, hardly a motivation to grind your way thru, just for different pictures, no matter how cute.
If this were a mini-game in a larger role-playing or dungeon diving game I would think it was awesome, but as a stand alone, yeah, I paid three bucks, more than got my moneys worth, but it isn't anything special.

I bought this game with the intention of completing all of its achievements, and unfortunately that will be influencing my review. I wanted to wait until I was finished the achievements, but my frustration with them is overflowing.

The game is fine enough. A little light on content, even for what it is and the price it's at. The achievements add a bit to that though. The majority of them add a little challenge that isn't too unrealistic to accomplish. But then there's two of them that have me wanting to put my head through a wall. Winning a game with 250 gold, and getting to level 15 in Delve mode. 

I don't even really know where to begin with the 250 gold. I've gotten 178 I believe, and I had a really good run. I see that some people at least have this achievement though, which can't be said for the level 15 one. Delve mode is basically just consecutive games with random sets of ability cards each time, with each level requiring you to collect a certain amount of gold on top of winning to advance. When you lose, you go back down one level. 

This game has some level of skill required to understand what you need to do in certain situations, but more than that, you need luck. Good luck. Amazing luck. I've played this game for two full days now and have only gotten to level 14 ten times. Six of those times, I lost on the second turn. No options, no choice but to take enough damage to kill me, six times. Another three of those times I won without enough gold, which might actually be more frustrating, believe it or not. Only one time did I lose because I made a mistake, and even then, I probably didn't have enough gold to make it in the end. When I'm not struggling on level 14, I'm going up and down levels 9 through 13 for hours. It's not fun. Had I known completing this game would require this amount of luck based grinding, I wouldn't have bothered with it at all. Solitaire games are inherently luck based, and I understand that, but this is a ridiculous expectation for an achievement, in my opinion. I can't say for sure that I feel the same about the 250 gold one because I've spent much less time on it, but so far it's been frustrating as well.

The presentation is nice, and the game has a charm to it, but I don't feel that it's enough, personally. If you're interested in completing the game, don't. It's become such an awful chore. [h1]TL;DR[/h1]

Fun card game with a blend of strategy and RNG, but needs a bit more depth. Inexpensive and offers potential for much more through DLC.

[h1]Full Review[/h1]

In a similar vein to games like [i]Solitairica[/i], [i]Card Crawl[/i] offers a lite fantasy setting, amusing visuals, and some replay value. Without going into too much detail, strategy fans may find things a bit lacking in terms of complexity and replayability, and too much reliance upon RNG. This could easily be solved by DLC that adds new challenges, character abilities and/or gameplay modes.

In particular, the inclusion of character abilities (both the player and the enemy) would add a whole lot to what is otherwise an amusing, lite CCG. This lack of depth is my main complaint, and while it may result in me spending few hours in the future playing. With that said, I play countless hours of [i]Freecell[/i] and [i]Spider Solitaire[/i], so I may yet prove myself wrong.

[u]Pros[/u]

[list]
 [*] Cheap, especially if you catch a sale
 [*] Lite strategy for when you like solitaire, but want something different
 [*] Great illustration and design work
 [*] Does allow for [i]some[/i] customization of decks
 [*] Offers a few modes of play, including a daily challenge
 [*] Steam Leaderboard for those that enjoy competitive play
[/list]

[u]Cons[/u]

[list]
 [*] Too much grind to unlock certain features, particularly with the lack of strategy available
 [*] Character quests offer visual differences only; potential for much more
 [*] Characters themselves are different in image only; compare with [i]Solitairica[/i] where each has different abilities
 [*] Some minor bugs ([i]e.g.[/i], Trophy room hangs as of this writing)
[/list]

[u]Scores[/u]

[list]
 [*] Graphics: 9/10
 [*] Audio: 8/10
 [*] Gameplay: 7/10
 [*] Replayability: 6/10
 [*] [b]Overall: 7.5/10[/b]
[/list]

Overall, if you're a fan of CCG and/or solitaire-style games, give this one a go. At less than $5 CDN, it's good bang for the buck. And hopefully more purchases will encourage the devs to add new functionality to a game that has lots of potential.

Card Crawl is a strategy based solitaire-like card game. Card crawl relies heavy on the RNG. 

A deck in this game has 54 cards. You have the following cards: Potions, shields, swords, monsters, coins and each draw you get 5 randomly selected ability cards.
You can unlock more and better ability cards in this game if you earn enough money.
You have 13 health points. Besides both sides of your portrait you have two hands and on the right there is a backpack slot for items. There is a box where you can discard cards. You cannot discard monster cards.
Each turn four cards are drawn. Three of those cards must be played before new cards will be drawn.
The goal is to have zero cards left. This means you have to survive for 54 cards. There is some strategy involved, but also a lot of luck.
The high score is based on how much money you have at the end of a game. This score can be used to buy new ability cards.

The game has a normal mode and a constructed mode. In the normal mode the 5 ability cards are randomly selected for you. In the constructed mode, you can choose 5 ability cards you want in your deck.
You also have your daily challenges.
And you have the Deck merchant mode: custom games made by other players. (you need to win 20 games to unlock it)
The game has a tutorial, which is a very good one.
Your progress is automatically saved.

Success in Card Crawl depends on what cards you are dealt, and how you choose to play them. There is some strategy involved and you do have to think about how you want to play your cards. There are also a lot of special ability cards that you can unlock as you continue to play and get better. The game’s randomness with regards to what cards you are dealt, and which special ability cards are also randomly chosen for you, provide tremendous replay value for Card Crawl. There are also extra gamemodes and characters that can be unlocked as well. This is a game that can be enjoyed in both short play sessions and long play sessions. There’s also a mobile version available for Android (on Google Play), and for iOS (on the App Store). Card Crawl is definitely one of the very best card based video games that there is. Card Crawl is a RPG card game where you try to clear cards. The objective is to clear all 54 cards in a deck consisting of items and monsters.

Gameplay-wise, use a mouse. You have 4 slots; 1 hero, 2 hands and 1 backpack. Each turn 4 cards are flipped over from the 54 card deck. You can only use 3 out of the 4 cards. Using a Monster will damage you. Using Items will reduce the damage or heal you. Try to survive by pitting Items vs Monsters and ensuring your life points do not hit 0. 

Combat follows rudimentary mathematics where you just add and minus. You start with a 13-life Knight. You basically ensure the damage does not kill you and your lifepoints do not hit 0. Monsters damage you according to their power. E.g. 10 power Soulstealer deals 10 damage to you. You can reduce the damage to you by attacking the monster with a weapon, healing with a potion after damage is dealt or blocking with a shield. Basically, item cards are add, monster cards are minus. Just make sure you don't hit 0. Occassionally, use abilities to do interesting actions. E.g. 

Conclusion, Card Crawl is oddly boring, so I wouldn't recommend it.

I said above that the developers of Pinball spent minimal time on “their” game. Now it is a simple game, and that isn't a bad thing with me. But there is so much that isn't well though out on this.

Pros:
1) It does have good art.
2) Does have decent pinball physics.

Cons:
1) Music seems a bit generic.
2) Each table (including ones you make) has goals.
3) Unable to rebind keys or use a controller. Heck the controls are bad!
4) The editor! My god this is bad!
5) No way to import models, artwork, music, or even sound.
6) Menus.

Now the physics are pretty good, and the art including isn't to bad, but the music is pretty generic and short. (Running the game in the background as I write this.) Now onto the bad things about this! This may get long!

Since I already discussed the music, I will start with the controls, you know, the thing that needs to be good! It is bad! Most of your controls are placed onto the arrow keys and camera set to A, S, D, Z, X and C  keys which is annoying. Rebinding these would have increased the game play massively for me on this. If this isn't bad, there is no controller support! Even I have controller support in the game I am making! Most engines of any type have some sort of way to code that in!

Now goals isn't the problem with me, but how they tell you when you get them not well thought out. When you complete so many goals, a voice will tell you "X percent", which can be kinda annoying. When you do complete them, it stops your game play to tell you that you completed the goals, and ask if you want to continue the table or go to the next. I will go to the next table next time I am ready, and I believe most do as well. Heck, it took me a couple of minutes to figure out these little stars are indeed goals, and never tells you that this is what your need to do.

Now I am going to skipped importing and the editor, these are kinda the same and will be discussed at the end.

The menus are terrible in here. Like there is a lack of them. When you start the game, you are jumped into a table with some boxes at top. That is your menu, folks! There is a couple of windows inside there, but to choose a table, you need to hit settings. Sorry baKno, this is not a setting, this is game play. No keybindings at all. Game just reloads the table you selected and lets you play. then you have editor which will let you into the editor, but can't all this be on something like a main menu? I would think it wouldn't be that difficult to program that! I have made many of them in all sort of languages that I coded in before.

Now with making tables. Now I would complain about workshop not being included, but this was released before that, so I will give this a pass on this. However! What I will not give a pass on is the controls. The NES has better controls, and that only had four face buttons and a d-pad. This has the entire keyboard and mouse. Panning, and zooming is all used with those same keys as before when playing the game, and mouse.  There is no categories for the parts in this, and you must drag the parts from the toolbar to the table. Some of the parts you use, like ramps, are a static model. Ramps should be molded to what you want them to be, not be a u-turn. You cannot change the sizes of the bumpers at all, and the color of the lights. The saucers are only for multi-balls. You cannot link any of the targets or lights, which are both targets. There are no flashing lights or regular lights that you can use. The artwork is only a generic looking table or one of the other ten table's artwork that you get in game. You cannot even change the music on any table. Just theme the look and that is all.
Importing is not an option, at all. I can kind of understand copyright, but make some more art if this is going to be the case or include decals, heck both, but still, you can put something in your EULA stating you are not responsible for what others put in the game. I have read that so many times, since I like games with editors, this is a disappointment.

A fantastic game for just having some fun and venting over whatever's on your mind.  It isn't without flaws of course (which I will point out further below here).

I honestly did not expect any sort of story mode so that was a fun bonus and a good way to get introduced to some of the weaponry.  It gets a bit more intense when the dummies start chasing after you.  Especially when they end up right behind you!  The gameplay in the story isn't the best part since the dummies end up just tripping themselves or get so close they sit right on top of you.  But it still makes for a fun experience.

The free mode is the most enjoyable.  Even with the dummies just sitting still, you can do as you please.  Get some new weapons, see how they work, throw the dummies around all you want!  It's too much fun to smack them everywhere.

That all being said, there are a few critiques I have that could easily be mended within any future updates.

1.  The sound effects need to be upgraded.  Sound work isn't easy, but when you hit a dummy with a barbed wire baseball bat, you expect at least some form of impact noise.  But sadly most of the melee weapons don't express anything like that (aside from boxing gloves and the brass knuckles, two of the most satisfying weapons to use due to that impacting thud).  The only sound you get is a light thud of the dummy hitting the floor.  It makes your attack feel so much less powerful!  A couple different sounds added in would really change that fact and make the game far more immersive as well as just plain satisfying.

2. Free mode Options.  In free mode, you get one dummy and one drone, but that's all.  I would like to see some more options to really give it that sandbox feel.  Something where you can select how many dummies or drones there are, where they're placed, if they are sentient or not and such.  It would be greatly interesting to see a sentient dummy who is not being aggressive but would turn so after being attacked.  Just another little something to add more flair to the mode.

3. Workshop support.  I was looking for it but did not see any form of workshop for the game.  In something like this, the steam community could really add to the features.  I can only imagine the crazy weapons that would come out of that workshop and they could even have set gold amounts to be unlocked as well to keep that mechanic in play.  

4. The Physics.  Perhaps not something that is needing to be "fixed" so much as just adjusted or even made adjustable.  It is really entertaining to send the dummies tumbling to the ground but with a few weapons it just feels a bit off.  They mostly react to you pushing them with the weapons more than the impact itself it feels.  I would expect a high speed swing of a baseball bat to really send them flying while a brass knuckle would put them on the ground in front of you.  If the weapons were given specific forces to affect how far the dummy goes, that would also add some fairly enjoyable reality to the game.  It is still hilarious to lift weapons from below and make them do cartwheels!

Overall, still a very fun game to enjoy.  With a few updates, it could be perfected into one satisfying way to vent!

[b] Purple Heart [/b] is what I call a platformer in a Meatboy genre. Unfortunately, I have lots of complaints other than high difficulty. There are some issues with controls and overall lack of intuitive mechanics.  Also, I would like to see a more satisfying death animation with a sound effect.

Issues that need to be addressed:

- jump button and activation button should not be the same
- some spawn points are in a way of danger 
- too much delay before sticking to a wall
- needs more air control when bouncing off walls 
- wall slide should be faster if I hold down
- the dash needs distance control like shorter range if you hold back
- visibility issues ( black spikes coming out of black walls with no indication, sometimes not in a predictable way) - This is not the kind of difficulty I look for

[h1] Final Thoughts 5/10 [/h1]

It can be a decent hardcore platformer with more polish. Music is very nice although I don't find the game particularly enjoyable visually (a little hard to see). Right now most of the difficulty comes from less than fluid controls and visibility problems.

Good concept, but the execution is lacking in many areas.  I liked the overall aesthetic with the pixel art style, and the lighting effects were atmospheric and thematic.  I lost interest quickly though as the controls were just too clunky.  It's a shame because I feel like this game could have been really good - especially for the cheap price tag.  A few points of feedback:

Jump and activate *need* to be a different button.  Several times I got stuck in an area where there was a console to activate, and short walls on both sides.  This is effectively a soft lock as you can't jump away with the console close enough to think you want to press the button again instead.

Need some control over the dash length - the times I got stuck in the corner with the console were due to the dash length being so long that it took me into the inescapable hole.

Jump physics could be better - the player character immediately stops drifting up once you let go of the jump button - this is unintuitive.

Wall jump controls are clunky.  As it is, holding towards the wall and jumping sends you straight out - a useless angle in most circumstances.  To jump up, you have to hold two keys.  To jump up and then out, you have to hold two keys, then swap one mid jump.  None of these are intuitive.  The mechanic is clearly inspired by Megaman X, and this game could do well to model after their walljump physics.

The developer mistakes lack of visual cues for "difficulty".  Hiding spikes behind the walls and not having them show up until you are close enough to die from it is not difficult - it's poor game design.  In a good game, the player can see a location/object and immediately tell whether or not it is safe to be there.  Consider dark souls.  The player is never wondering whether or not the monster with the giant pitchfork is going to hurt them.  The difficulty is not in identifying the threat, but rather with dealing with it.

Ironically, the game holds the players hand through things that are painfully obvious.  Example: there is a block with a skull on it.  Even if the player has never played a video game before, they should know better than to step on it, but the game unhelpfully reminds them not to anyway.

There are a few gramattical missteps in the dialogue as well.

It's for these reasons that I can't recommend this game.  Were the developer to release a patch that addressed the clunky controls, softlock issues, and problems with clarity, it would absolutely be worth the cheap price.

I've read over a dozen slice-of-life visual novels, and A Sky Full of Stars is undoubtedly my favorite. It does everything so well: characters, setting, and story. Few VNs had me fully engrossed in its world like ASFoS did.

One of my favorite things about this VN, is how concise the writing is. Visual novels (especially in the slice-of-life genre) are often guilty of dragging on with endless amounts of filler, but thankfully, it doesn't happen here. On the contrary, it feels like every sentence and every line of dialogue is written with a purpose, especially in the common route. As a result, this is one of the most information-dense VNs I've read, with the story and characters having far greater depth than most other VNs, even the longer ones. It's great that the writers respect the readers' time.

The characters are all likeable with a decent amount of depth. The protagonist and two main heroines are all given a backstory and their own motivation for their interest in astronomy. Even the side characters are well fleshed out. In addition, there's no overused shallow archetypes present. For once in a VN, the protagonist's male best friend is not a joke character, and even the useless-single-adult-woman character has a decent amount of depth.

I thought a story about astronomy would be simple, but it was a lot more interesting and complex than I imagined. The story spans six years, starting from elementary school all the way till high school. At any given time, there's usually multiple events interacting and happening at the same time, and before I knew it, I was fully engrossed in the events. Even as somebody with no interest or prior knowledge in astronomy, I still found the cast's passion for astronomy rubbing off on me, and I felt like I was part of the astronomy club, sharing the same victories and setbacks.

Compared to other slice-of-life VNs, this is easily one of the most serious in tone, with the least amount of comedy. It's also one of the most realistic and least "pandery". The enjoyment primarily comes from watching the cast bond over a shared interest, grow, work hard, overcome obstacles, and achieve their goals. I find this much more preferable to the comedy-heavy VNs that rely on a series of one-off jokes. (Of course, your mileage may vary.)

The music, while not the best, serves its purpose. The calm music, combined with the starry night sky background that's frequently shown, often make me forget I'm trapped on this tiny planet, and instead feel like I'm going on a journey through space with the cast.

You may have heard about the controversy regarding MoeNovel's translation of If My Heart Had Wings. But don't worry- the translation of A Sky Full of Star sis actually decent. Everything makes sense, nothing is butchered in order to appeal to 12 year old French girls. The only real issue I've noticed is that the translation doesn't respect Japanese honorifics, and just uses people's first names. But that's not a big issue, and hardly detracts from the fact that the story is one of the best. This is an easy recommend for anyone interested in slice-of-life visual novels.

This is excellent. I used to do this spooky stuff all the time back in '01-'03, and this pretty neatly sums up the paranormal investigator lifestyle.

You start out broke and ill-equipped, trespassing on private property and scaring yourself witless with every creak and gust of wind. Once the fear is too much you hightail it back to your truck and gtfo. You use the exp gained to bring better gear the next time.

Maybe then you start to get really brave and spend time chatting with ghosts or scouring for evidence, and the threat becomes real. The monsters you'd heard about in the scattered lore are now somewhere on the property actively seeking you out.  You have to try to document these things without letting them get ahold of you. You'll eventually gain access to a crafting station where you can make traps and totems to use against the monsters. 

It turns into a deadly game of paparazzi hide and seek. You're trying to draw out the evil ones into your camera equipment and traps while keeping yourself alive and sane. Each creature has a unique behavior you must learn to recognize and exploit. Then you have to make it back to your truck with all your evidence.

Really great experience, especially considering it's still developing. Strongly recommend. UPDATE 0.6 REVIEW EDIT ADDED.

If you're thinking about buying this, hold off for now. Here's why:

The days are impossibly short. I have played 2 real time hours and 4 game days have elapsed, but died 6 times and had to restart from a previous save each time. So at a guess I will say that each day is about 15  real minutes long. This gives you no time to try and explore the 16km2 of island before it gets too dark. I ventured off to retrieve an air drop 850m away and it was dark just as I returned. There's no way you can go to the other side of this island to explore without a huge risk of dying and having to revert to a previous save.
0.2 EDIT: A small improvement, but still too short. Seeing the day counter in the top left I'm going to assume that your time on the island is limited to 360 days. At the rate in which the days elapse this will be a short sentence and game.

The food ratios are imbalanced. There's a carbs/protein/water system in place which is impossible to manage. The carbs are too difficult to find. I found one corn plant in 4 in game days, and this is hardly enough to keep your carb levels in balance. If you're going to implement this system then make the required nutrition available. During this time I was taking health hits due to a zero carb level.
0.2 EDIT: I found two corn plants on a bare hill. Nowhere near enough to survive. If you're going to be dropped on an island to survive your incarceration, then food should be available otherwise it's a death sentence. The threat should come from enemy inmates, not food shortage.

There are coconuts to eat but they give you minimal carb nutrition but hit you with a 15 point sickness level, I have no idea why they make you sick. The water system is also unbalanced. I found 2 watermelons in the same timeframe which didn't go far at all. You can use coconuts for water but again, they make you sick. Pacific islanders live on this s##t.
0.2 EDIT: These still make you sick for some stupid reason, and I found no watermelons at all. This is just f#####g ridiculous, they may as well be removed from the game.

The stamina system is also flawed. You can run for 5 seconds, then have to walk for 2 seconds. Am I that unfit that I can't run for more than 5 seconds?
0.2 EDIT: Added to initial review.

You can't pause the game. If you want to take a toilet break, then exit the game otherwise the timer keeps on counting down. If you're near your base and can save and exit, then any air drops that have not been collected are lost as the locations don't save with the game.
0.2 EDIT: Still no pause. You still lose all acquired POI marks.

The enemies advance a vastly superior rate than you do. In trying to retrieve an air drop I was attacked by an armed inmate, and I was still in the stone age. As I was cracking him in the skull he was able to reload and continue firing. I was able to bring him down but the firearm he was using to beat me down to 11 health had mysteriously vanished, he was using it, why can't I?. I also approached an enemy camp and was surprised to find 2 inmates armed with pistols with a 4x4 base, and I still only had a lean-to shelter.
0.2 EDIT: I wasn't able to approach an enemy base. A POI marker came up, but I wanted to save and restart from a previous save to try and sort out the building bug and lost the location of the camp.

There's no map. How do I know where I've been or the where the locations are of any POI's that I've come across? In game I can make a multitude of incredible things like buckets, and forge metals, but I can't use some charcoal and a piece of cloth to map out my progress.

An amazing JRPG game and incredible series. Everything from world building to characters make it shine and lovable.

It's not as good as the first game but it's still pretty dang good. I already gushed over the story and gameplay of the first. Here is how things have changed slightly since then:

Story: 
The story of this game takes place right after the first (or 3 months after I think? I forgot). It's divided into act 1 and act 2 with an intermission. Act 1 is peak. It really captures the same feelings that I had in the first game and really shows the consequences of the first game. Act 2... is alright. Once the band is back together the story devolves into a save the world type deal that's desperately trying to pretend it's not. So there's that.

Gameplay:
There are two distinct changes to the gameplay that leave me feeling mixed. The first is mech combat. The mech combat... is fine. It's basically rock-paper-scissors. Though there is the edition of more skills based on which party members you have which is pretty cool. I don't think it overstays it's welcome too, usually happening at the end of a chapter.

The 2nd is overdrive. Overdrive is one of the most fun mechanics ever. In any jrpg. Why yes I do want 3 free turns back to back. That said it's also incredibly broken in favor of the paper due to the fact that it makes arts instant. There are some spells you get from hidden bosses and these are basically screen nukes with large cast times. Overdrive let's you do it instantly. That said it also can be used in different ways such as curing teammates of status conditions, but I still think it's too broken.

Speaking of too broken. Rean suffers from some major protagonist privilege in this game. He get's a super mode (teased in the first game) and later you can even summon your mech to fight (albeit in non-story combat). I liked Rean in the first game and his focus on delaying enemies. But I could see myself not using him. Now there is no reason not to use him and I get annoyed when jrpgs have large rosters but one character you absolutely need to have all the time.

Additionally, dedicated tanks feel like a thing of the past when Jusis can grant everyone physical and magical immunity on a craft. 

Misc:
The now open map of Erebonia is great to explore since you only got to see snippets in the first game. Though it runs the issue of having too much to do when you reach the endgame. Hidden quests, quests that only pop up when you talk to a specific npc with no indication, become a chore to discover without a guide.

So yeah. This is a solid 8/10.
